criterion.note: Lift is precision at the default tier divided by the area's own base rate. Conakry measured 0.584 / 0.261 = 2.24x. A second town at or above 1.5x supports a national screening layer with the tier and recall caveats already documented; below that it should stay a per-city tool.
criterion.known_defect: Lift is capped at 1/base_rate, so a grid over a dirtier town is scored against a lower ceiling for reasons that have nothing to do with the model: 3.83x at 26% prevalence, 2.29x at 44%. ROC-AUC would have been the base-rate-invariant choice. This is left as declared because it was fixed before any second grid existed and changing it afterwards is the exact freedom pre-declaration removes -- but `evaluate` now prints the invariant comparison beside the verdict, and a FAIL here must not be read as 'discrimination got worse'.
